_why: Station 04 covers ONE named sweep per run, completely, instead of every sweep shallowly. Without recorded state every fresh run picks the first entry, which narrows coverage without rotating it - gate liveness gets checked forever and instruction drift never does. This file is that state. Station 04 reads it, runs the sweep it names, then advances it via: node scripts/pipeline/next-sweep.mjs --advance

sweeps.title: Gate liveness
sweeps.brief: Execute every armed and HOLD prompt's premise against origin/main at a named SHA. A premise that returns false is finished work still sitting on the board. Repair dead requires_merged / requires_file_on_main / requires_on_main gates - and re-check the prompts behind each one you repair, because a dead gate MASKS the premise behind it.

sweeps.title: Instrument honesty
sweeps.brief: Take DOCTRINE section 9 and prove each trap is still trapped. Run the query that lies (ls-tree without -r, git status against a gitignored file, gh run list --branch main, a --jq string through the shell) and confirm the documented failure still reproduces. A trap that has been fixed upstream and still reads as live is itself drift. Report anything section 9 claims that you cannot reproduce.

sweeps.title: Repo hygiene
sweeps.brief: Orphaned worktrees and their locks, stash growth in the watcher clone, superseded prompt files littering the queue root, tracked *-ready.md at depth 1 (the board trap), branches merged but not deleted, and HOLD files tracked on main whose work has already shipped. REPORT ONLY - stage a prompt for anything worth deleting. No agent bulk-deletes.

sweeps.title: Instruction drift
sweeps.brief: Diff each scheduled-task bootstrap under C:\Users\Marco\Claude\Scheduled against the repo station doc it points at. Confirm station_doc_version matches on both sides. Run lint-station.mjs. Check every path DOCTRINE and the station docs name still resolves. This sweep exists because five pasted copies drifted for weeks and four carried advice this pipeline had already disproved.
